title: Derivative at a point: two equivalent limit forms
ced_evidence: CHA-2.B.1: "These are equivalent forms of the definition of the derivative" (provided the limit exists)

title: Calculator answers: rounding
body: Present the expression you evaluated on the calculator, round or truncate to three places after the decimal point, and store intermediate calculations to avoid accumulated rounding error.
ced_evidence: Preparing for the AP Exam: "rounding or truncating to three places after the decimal point"; CHA-2.D.2

title: Keep notation precise: parentheses and defined names
body: Write derivatives with standard notation (f′(x), y′, or dy/dx), keep parentheses around grouped factors, and do not rename a derivative to a new symbol without defining it.
ced_evidence: Skill 4.C "Use appropriate mathematical symbols and notation"; CHA-2.B.3; "students may drop important notation, such as a parenthesis"

title: Derivatives of sin x, cos x, e^x, ln x
ced_evidence: FUN-3.A.4: "Specific rules can be used to find the derivatives for sine, cosine, exponential, and logarithmic functions."

title: Quotient rule
caution: The numerator order matters (the denominator's factor times u′ comes first). Show this rule structure as a separate step before substituting values.
ced_evidence: FUN-3.B.2: "Derivatives of quotients of differentiable functions can be found using the quotient rule."

title: Product rule
caution: The derivative of a product is not the product of the derivatives. Show the product rule structure, e.g. f′(3) = u(3)v′(3) + v(3)u′(3), before substituting values.
ced_evidence: FUN-3.B.1: "Derivatives of products of differentiable functions can be found using the product rule"; "f ′(3) = u(3)v′(3) + v(3)u′(3)"

title: Evaluate a limit by recognizing a derivative
body: If a limit has the form of the difference quotient defining the derivative of a function whose derivative is known, evaluate the limit as that derivative at the indicated point.
ced_evidence: LIM-3.A.1: "recognizing an expression for the definition of the derivative of a function whose derivative is known offers a strategy for determining a limit"
